title: Starlight escalation roster & late-shift notes (2026-08-15)
content:
Context:
- Shift window: 02:00–10:00 PDT (late APAC overlap). Light traffic until 03:10 when tokenizing latency spike observed for hosted/text-generation endpoints.
- Affected surfaces: /v1/generate and streaming sockets (ws-gateway). No authentication failures observed.
- Initial hypothesis: degraded KV-cache eviction + hot-shard on a small subset of Dedicated pools after a deployment.

What we observed (timeline):
- 03:10: alert: 5xx rate increased from baseline 0.03% -> 0.8% in 3m (alert SRE-4129).
- 03:12: sharp increase in p99 latency from 220ms -> 1.8s for short-context requests (<256 tokens).
- 03:15: ops page and #sre-oncall notified automatically; staggered push to late-shift roster.
- 03:18: manual check: majority of 5xx were 502 gateway + 504 upstream timeouts; no DB errors in telemetry.
- 03:22: deployed rollback flagged as possible cause (infra PR merged 02:58) — rollback considered.
- 03:28: attempted soft-mitigation: increased request-timeout for ws-gateway to 45s and reduced concurrent connections to affected pool. Minimal effect.
- 03:38: devs and infra started controlled rollback of PR #628 to a canary subset.
- 03:50: canary rollback cut error-rate by ~60% within 7 minutes.
- 04:05: full rollout rollback completed; p99 returned to 260–320ms by 04:12.

Actions taken (chronological):
1) Triage: verified alert, collected logs (gateway + worker traces), and correlated with deployment timeline.
2) Short mitigation: adjusted ws-gateway timeouts and connection caps to reduce queueing.
3) Canary rollback of infra PR #628, observed improvement -> rollback full.
4) Post-rollback: restarted two affected dedicated pools to ensure clean cache state.
5) Stakeholder comms: posted summary to #infra-ops and incident thread, paged on-call rotation.

Open follow-ups (owners + due dates):
- Investigate why KV-cache eviction behavior regressed after PR #628 (owner: Ravi Patel, due: 2026-08-20).
- Add synthetic test for short-context p99 on canary runs (owner: Lin Chen, due: 2026-08-22).
- Tighten pre-merge inference smoke for ws-gateway under connection pressure (owner: Marcus O'Hara, due: 2026-08-19).
- Update runbook: "ws-gateway-partial-outage" with rollback checklist and timeout knobs (owner: Ava Martinez, due: 2026-08-18).

Runbook notes / proposed edits:
- Current runbook lacks an explicit check for recent infra merges when p99 latency spikes. Add a step: verify commit windows in last 60m and cross-check canary health before scaling pools.
- Add a quick command list to evict/rehydrate KV-cache safely (examples + minimum safe concurrency) — see Confluence: ops/runbooks/kv-cache-recovery.
- Add a recommended emergency switch: "force-canary-rollback" play that automates canary cut and alert suppression for 30m.

Lessons & hypotheses:
- Root cause likely interaction between new connection-handling logic in PR #628 and cache eviction timing that produced transient head-of-line blocking on worker processes.
- Rollbacks are still the fastest reliable mitigation; we should instrument canary rollbacks with automatic traffic cut indicators for faster confidence.
- Observability gap: missing synthetic that exercises small-sequence token flows at production concurrency levels.

Notes to next shift / handoff checklist:
- Key artifacts: logs uploaded to S3 bucket s3://ops-logs/2026-08-15/starlight (grep: ws-gateway, pr-628), traces linked in the incident thread.
- Runbook to run if symptoms reappear: ops/runbooks/ws-gateway-partial-outage (temp changes documented in this doc).
- Contact ladder: on-call (Ava Martinez), primary infra lead (Ravi Patel), serving-runtime (Lin Chen), on-call manager (Marcus O'Hara). Pager escalation rules applied.
- Pending merges to watch: infra PR #631 (connection pooling adjustments) — hold until KV-cache test exists.

Post-incident retrospective items (for next retro):
- Short write-up of timeline and mitigation (owner: Ava) to be attached to JIRA SRE-4129.
- Add 2 small synthetic workloads to CI that exercise <256-token p99 under moderate parallelism.
- Discuss adding automated canary rollback policy in staging to reduce time-to-mitigation.

Misc / random notes to self:
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C01234567/p1692110400000 (incident thread).
- Observed oddity: a single Dedicated shard reported higher socket backlog despite even traffic distribution — follow-up with infra sharding team.
- Control-plane audit: verify there were no KV-cache TTL changes in the deploys (owner: Ravi).

Summary (TL;DR):
A recent infra merge (PR #628) introduced a regression in connection handling that amplified KV-cache eviction side-effects, producing transient p99 latency spikes and 5xxs for short-context requests. Canary rollback mitigated quickly; next steps are runbook updates, targeted tests, and follow-up investigations assigned above.

End of notes.
